result.title: Simulation Priors for Rapid Adaptation in Model-Based RL for Autonomous Racing
result.summary: Reinforcement learning enables learning high-performance control policies, but its reliance on extensive interaction limits deployment on physical systems where data collection is costly, and failures are unsafe. We introduce Prior-Informed Adaptation (PIA), an offline-to-online model-based RL framework that uses structured simulation priors for rapid adaptation. PIA pretrains a world model on heterogeneous low- and high-fidelity simulated trajectories, then adapts it with limited target-domain interaction using uncertainty-regularized planning. Rather than requiring an accurate simulator for policy transfer, PIA treats simulated trajectories as biased priors whose residual mismatch is corrected during online adaptation. We evaluate PIA in autonomous racing using high-fidelity simulation and on a real full-size autonomous race car. In simulation, PIA adapts faster across track and surface shifts than strong baselines, achieving lower lap times and fewer failures. On hardware, PIA achieves reliable few-shot adaptation with less than one hour of on-vehicle interaction.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 PIA 框架：用低/高保真仿真轨迹预训练世界模型，再通过不确定性正则化规划在目标域少量交互下快速适配，并在自动驾驶赛车的仿真与实车上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将仿真轨迹视为有偏先验、在线校正残差，以及隐状态世界模型加不确定性驱动规划的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的训练监督、分布偏移下的状态更新与不确定性决策提供可核查线索。
